level1.text: The mass of an object is $4.0\,\text{kg}$. What is its weight on Earth?
The spring of a force meter stretches 2.0 cm when an object with a weight of 4.0 N is hung on it. How many centimetres does the spring stretch when an object with a weight of 12 N is hung on it?
The mass of a measuring instrument left on the surface of the Moon is $30\,\text{kg}$. What is its weight on the Moon? Read the value of $g$ from the table of the lesson.
The graph shows the calibration measurements of the spring of a force meter. When an unknown object is hung on the spring, it stretches $3.5\,\text{cm}$. How great a force stretches the spring?
The mass of an object is $2.5\,\text{kg}$. What is its weight on Jupiter, where $g = 24.8\,\text{m/s}^2$?

level2.text: A force meter shows 49 N when an object is hung on it on Earth. What is the mass of the object?
The mass of a hen's egg is $60\,\text{g}$. What is its weight on Earth in newtons?
The mass of an astronaut with equipment is $145\,\text{kg}$. By how much is his weight on the Moon ($g = 1.62\,\text{m/s}^2$) smaller than on Earth ($g = 9.81\,\text{m/s}^2$)?
The spring of a force meter stretches 1.5 cm when a $0.20\,\text{kg}$ object is hung on it on Earth. How great a force stretches the spring 4.5 cm?

level3.text: An object is hung on a force meter on Earth, and the meter shows 18 N. The same object is taken to Mars ($g = 3.71\,\text{m/s}^2$). What does the same meter show there?

On Earth a lifter can lift at most a mass of $22.0\,\text{kg}$, that is, the lifter can produce a force equal to the weight of this mass. How great a mass could the lifter lift on the Moon ($g = 1.62\,\text{m/s}^2$) with the same force?

The scale of a force meter has been made on Earth so that it shows, in kilograms, the number obtained by dividing the force by $9.81\,\text{m/s}^2$. On Mars ($g = 3.71\,\text{m/s}^2$) the meter shows $26\,\text{kg}$ for an object hung on it. What is the mass of the object?
